conclusion: Previous demonstrations of contextuality-type obstruction start from quantum mechanics or from externally specified measurement scenarios. We show that the same locally-Boolean-but-globally-obstructed structure can arise from an autonomous emergence framework—Six Birds Theory—without importing Hilbert space, amplitudes, or the Born rule. The formal vehicle is a finite event package: a family of stable-record contexts, each carrying a finite Boolean event algebra, together with a layer-relative shared-event identification and an audit layer. Obstruction is the failure of admissible global realization for that package. The computational framework combines exact and quotient-backed feasibility, structural and statistical deficits, provenance auditing, and false-positive controls. The evidence base includes a classical control, a boundary-case epistemic calibration, an explicit finite parity/context witness, and autonomous discovery organized by mechanism, lens, and packaging axes. The results are stratified: mechanism variation yields package-sensitive structure with a quotient-backed witness under a weaker claim ceiling; lens variation closes with a cross-resolution strict extension obstruction on fixed support; and packaging variation produces the strongest current obstruction, subject to a package conflict caveat. Where applicable, the principal cases persist under bounded robustness checks. The paper therefore provides the first computationally explicit evidence that contextuality-type obstruction can emerge from a system's own packaging structure rather than from quantum theory or an externally imposed scenario.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
An \emph{admissible global realization} of an event package
\[
\mathfrak{E}=(\mathcal C,\{B_c\}_{c\in\mathcal C},\sim,\mathcal A)
\]
consists of a finite set \(\Omega\) and maps \(\pi_c:\Omega\to A_c\) for all \(c\in\mathcal C\) such that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Context coverage.} For every \(c\in\mathcal C\) and every atom \(a\in A_c\), there exists \(\omega\in\Omega\) with \(\pi_c(\omega)=a\).
    \item \textbf{Event realization.} Each context event \(E\in B_c\) is realized by \(\mathopen{[\mkern-3mu[} E \rrbracket_\Omega^c\subseteq \Omega\).
    \item \textbf{Shared-event consistency.} Whenever \(E\in B_c\), \(F\in B_d\), and \(E\sim F\), one has
    \[
    \mathopen{[\mkern-3mu[} E \rrbracket_\Omega^c = \mathopen{[\mkern-3mu[} F \rrbracket_\Omega^d.
    \]
    \item \textbf{Audit admissibility.} The realization respects the package discipline encoded in \(\mathcal A\): no unlicensed hidden distinctions are introduced, and the realization remains within the layer's admissible record and interface class.
\end{enumerate}

source_wording_tex:
An \emph{admissible global realization} of an event package
\[
\EventPackage=(\mathcal C,\{B_c\}_{c\in\mathcal C},\sim,\mathcal A)
\]
consists of a finite set \(\Omega\) and maps \(\pi_c:\Omega\to A_c\) for all \(c\in\mathcal C\) such that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Context coverage.} For every \(c\in\mathcal C\) and every atom \(a\in A_c\), there exists \(\omega\in\Omega\) with \(\pi_c(\omega)=a\).
    \item \textbf{Event realization.} Each context event \(E\in B_c\) is realized by \(\llbracket E \rrbracket_\Omega^c\subseteq \Omega\).
    \item \textbf{Shared-event consistency.} Whenever \(E\in B_c\), \(F\in B_d\), and \(E\sim F\), one has
    \[
    \llbracket E \rrbracket_\Omega^c = \llbracket F \rrbracket_\Omega^d.
    \]
    \item \textbf{Audit admissibility.} The realization respects the package discipline encoded in \(\mathcal A\): no unlicensed hidden distinctions are introduced, and the realization remains within the layer's admissible record and interface class.
\end{enumerate}

\]
and every context is locally classical in the finite Boolean sense.

\paragraph{Proof sketch of \Cref{thm:shared-event-quotient}.}
The theorem is conditional on the admissibility and Boolean-stability of the shared-event relation on the relevant fixed comparison object. Under that assumption, if \(E_1\sim F_1\) and \(E_2\sim F_2\), then admissible probes and downstream identifications cannot distinguish the left and right unions either, so \(E_1\cup E_2\sim F_1\cup F_2\). Likewise, if \(E\sim F\), then admissible Boolean complementation on the local event algebras preserves the identification. The quotient is therefore stable under the local Boolean operations that the theorem uses. \qed

\paragraph{Proof sketch of \Cref{thm:shared-event-quotient}.}
The theorem is conditional on the admissibility and Boolean-stability of the shared-event relation on the relevant fixed comparison object. Under that assumption, if \(E_1\SharedEventEq F_1\) and \(E_2\SharedEventEq F_2\), then admissible probes and downstream identifications cannot distinguish the left and right unions either, so \(E_1\cup E_2\SharedEventEq F_1\cup F_2\). Likewise, if \(E\SharedEventEq F\), then admissible Boolean complementation on the local event algebras preserves the identification. The quotient is therefore stable under the local Boolean operations that the theorem uses. \qed
